extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation by Large Language Models (LLMs). It comprises 1,825 executable queries covering nine primary topics: Game Development, SVG Generation, Web Applications, Simulations, Data Science, Management Systems, Multimedia Editing, Quick Tools, and Others. The framework renders each artifact and captures its dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots, which are then assessed by a Multimodal LLM (MLLM)-as-Judge guided by a fine-grained, per-task checklist. Tasks are stratified into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers (559/611/655).
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Candidates were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness). Experts rewrote prompts for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting added diverse styles; humans verified.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis, Others
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query generation from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Prompt rewriting by experts for clarity/completeness/executability, followed by LLM rewriting to add diverse styles, and human verification. Tasks solved only by brittle hacks (e.g., hard-coded coordinates) were revised or removed.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items were re-authored or discarded. Automated filters dropped incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Solvability validation via candidate solutions from multiple model families with pruning of underspecified items.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. LLM (Hunyuan-Turbos) drafts the checklist, then humans refine for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration. The 10 items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions. Difficulty tiers (Easy/Medium/Hard) are assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ LLMs. Sub-categories are tagged by a lightweight classifier with human spot-checks. For validation, a 280-instance double-blind human study was conducted with multiple front-end engineers, using median of individual annotators' ratings as ground-truth.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Playwright (headless Chromium) at 1024×768 resolution for execution and screenshot capture.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A 10% manually curated seed achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators. For human validation, pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was computed between MLLM referee and human experts, achieving up to 90.95% agreement. Dual-referee setup (Gemini-2.5-Pro and Qwen2.5-VL-72B) yields highly consistent partial-order constraints over model rankings.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each query paired with one 10-dimension checklist; human validation study used multiple front-end engineers with median aggregation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Front-end engineers with extensive front-end development experience (for human validation study of 280 queries).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos (for checklist drafting), Gemini-2.5-Pro (MLLM-as-Judge referee), Qwen2.5-VL-72B (MLLM-as-Judge referee), Playwright with headless Chromium (execution harness), MinHash (for de-duplication), lightweight classifier (for sub-category tagging).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results are open-sourced at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io. Authors note version stability: replacing deprecated Gemini-2.5-Pro-Preview-0506 with stable Gemini-2.5-Pro yields identical ordering constraints.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Queries are explicitly filtered to avoid requesting or involving any sensitive personal information such as phone numbers, addresses, or other identifiable details (Privacy dimension in query quality filtering).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark aims to provide a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models, helping measure qualities that affect real-world user experience and adoption of interactive visual artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The methodology evaluates dynamic behavior by capturing and analyzing a sequence of screenshots at fixed intervals, which may not fully capture highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. The benchmark focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn, not agentic or iterative development capabilities (multi-turn self-debugging, autonomous refinement). MLLM referees can suffer from hallucination, prompt sensitivity, limited awareness of engineering/code quality, and version drift.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation/Testing benchmark for Large Language Models on interactive visual artifact generation. Used for benchmarking 30+ leading LLMs with fine-grained diagnostics across nine domains and three difficulty tiers (Easy/Medium/Hard).
